transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, doctor, thank you for seeing me. I know you're very busy. I'm Ruben, by the way. I, uh... I suppose I'm here because things have just felt a little off lately. I mean, nothing I can't handle, I'm sure, but my wife thought it would be good to come in. 

Most days I wake up with this... I guess you could call it a heavy, hollow feeling in my chest. It's silly, really. But it's like the old Ruben—the guy who could talk to anybody and just enjoy his day—is just... gone. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining that right. I don't want to make a big fuss out of nothing.
How long have you been feeling this way, Ruben?

Well, it's... it's been a little while now. Maybe around eight months or so? I hope I should have come in sooner, I'm sorry if I let it drag on too long. 

It kind of started around the time we got a new regional manager at work. I'm in sales, you see, and... well, he started coming down on me pretty hard, taking away some of the accounts I'd been handling for years. I know change is just part of the business, and I'm sure he has his reasons, but... I guess it just took the wind out of my sails more than I'd like to admit. Is it normal to let something like that get to you for so long?
Ruben, have you noticed yourself losing interest in activities or things you used to enjoy, like hobbies or spending time with friends or family?

Well, I... I suppose so, yes. I hope it doesn't sound like I'm just being lazy, I really don't mean to be. But, um... I used to really look forward to things, you know? Like my bowling league, or getting out and working in the garden. And my wife, she loves those gallery shows, and we used to go dancing... 

But lately, I just... I don't know, I just sit there and find myself making excuses not to go. It just doesn't feel worth the effort anymore, if that makes sense? I know I should be doing those things, especially for her. I feel terrible about it, really. Do you think that's something I can fix if I just try harder?
Ruben, do you find yourself feeling down or depressed most of the time, even when there's no clear reason for it?

Yes, doctor... I guess it goes back to what I was trying to say right at the beginning. I hope I'm not repeating myself too much, I'm sorry. But that... that heavy, hollow feeling in my chest? It's just there almost all the time now. 

Even on a perfectly fine day when I have absolutely no right to be upset, I just wake up with it. It really does feel like the old Ruben is just completely gone, and I can't even figure out why. I know I have a lot to be thankful for, a good wife, a steady job... so I feel awful even admitting that I feel so down when there's no real reason for it. Does that make sense? I hope I don't just sound incredibly ungrateful.
Ruben, have you noticed that you feel tired or that you've been lacking energy almost every day, even if you've had enough rest?

Well, um... I wouldn't say I'm completely lacking energy, no. I mean, I still get up and go to work every day, and I try my best to keep up with things around the house. I hope I'm not giving the impression that I'm just lying in bed all day, because I really do try to push through it. 

I guess maybe I get a little winded sometimes, or I might need an extra cup of coffee in the afternoon, but... isn't that just a normal part of getting a bit older? I'm 58 now, after all. I'm sure it's nothing to worry about, right? I try to stay as active as I can, I really do.
Ruben, have you found yourself feeling like you're not good enough, or that you're letting people down, even if you can't point to a clear reason for it?

Well... I mean, I really hope I don't come across as someone who just throws a pity party for himself, because I know I should be stronger than this. But, um... yes, I do feel that way. A lot, actually. 

I just... I keep telling myself I'm useless now. I've spent all these years taking care of my clients, you know, providing for my family, being the one they could rely on. And now... now I feel like none of that even counts anymore, because I can't even seem to handle my job the way I used to. I feel like I'm letting everyone down, especially my wife. It's embarrassing to admit that out loud, honestly. I'm sorry if that sounds pathetic... do you think it's normal to feel like such a failure when you're going through a rough patch like this?
Ruben, have you noticed that you're moving more slowly than usual, or maybe fidgeting and unable to sit still, even when you're not trying to?

Oh, no, I don't think so. I mean, I try to keep a pretty steady pace, you know? I wouldn't say I'm moving slowly or anything like that. I still get around just fine. 

And as for fidgeting... well, I hope I'm not fidgeting right now! I try to be respectful and pay attention when people are talking to me. I guess maybe I might tap my foot if I'm waiting in line or something, but that's just normal impatience, right? I don't think anyone would look at me and think I'm acting strange or restless. I'm doing my best to just be normal, I promise. Does it seem like I'm moving okay to you?
Ruben, would you say that you no longer take pleasure in things you used to enjoy, even the little things that used to make you smile or feel happy?

Well, I... I really don't want to sound like a stick in the mud, you know? I still try to be good company for my wife. But, um... I guess if I'm being completely honest, I haven't been doing much of what I used to love. 

I used to really look forward to going bowling, or getting outside and working in the garden. And I always loved taking my wife out to gallery shows or going dancing with her. Lately, though... I just kind of sit there. I end up making up excuses not to go, because... well, none of it really feels worth the effort right now. 

I feel terrible admitting that out loud, because I know I should be taking her out and doing those things. I hope that doesn't make me sound like a bad husband. It's probably just a phase, right? Everyone gets a little burnt out on their hobbies sometimes, don't you think? I really am trying my best to get back into the swing of things, I promise.
Ruben, can you recall if there's been any activity or moment recently, even something small, that has genuinely lifted your mood or brought you some sense of pleasure?

Well, I... I try to look for the silver lining, you know? I really do. I don't want to be the kind of person who just complains all the time. But... um... if I'm being honest, I can't really think of anything lately that's... well, that's made me feel good. 

I know I should be able to appreciate the little things, like a nice dinner my wife makes, or a sunny day, but it just... it all feels kind of flat. I feel awful saying that, like I'm ungrateful or something. I'm really not trying to be difficult. I just... I haven't felt that spark in a while. I hope that's an okay answer... do you think it's normal to just feel kind of numb to everything for a bit?

Ruben, when you say that nothing has genuinely lifted your mood recently, does that mean that even things you used to love, like spending time with your wife or enjoying a nice moment, don’t bring you any real joy anymore?

Well, yes... I suppose that's exactly what I meant earlier. I really hate having to say it again, because it just makes me sound so awful. But, um... yeah, like I was mentioning before about the bowling, or... or getting out in the garden. Even taking my wife to those gallery shows or going dancing... I just don't feel that joy from it at all right now. 

Instead of going out and enjoying it, I just sit there. I end up making up all these excuses to stay home because... well, getting up and doing it just doesn't feel worth the effort anymore. 

I really hope that doesn't make me sound like a terrible person. I love her very much, and I want to be a good husband, I really do. I'm just... struggling to find the fun in those things right now. I'm trying my best to fix it, though. I'm answering your questions okay, right? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need to hear.
Ruben, have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight lately—like eating much less or much more than usual?

Well, I... I try to make sure I eat enough to keep my energy up, you know? My wife is a wonderful cook, and I always want to show my appreciation for her meals. I really don't want to seem ungrateful or like I'm wasting food. 

But, um... if I'm being completely honest, I haven't really noticed any big changes. I mean, my clothes still fit about the same, I think. I haven't been stepping on the scale or anything, but I don't feel like I've gained or lost a bunch of weight. And I'm still eating... maybe not always with the biggest appetite, but I make sure to get something down. 

I hope that's the kind of information you were looking for? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right details. It's pretty normal for appetite to fluctuate a little bit as you get older, right? I'm sure I'm doing okay in that department.
Ruben, have you noticed any changes in your sleep lately—like trouble falling asleep, waking up during the night, or waking up earlier than usual and not being able to go back to sleep?

Well, I... I try to get a good night's rest, I really do. I know how important it is to be sharp for work, and I don't want to be dragging around the house, making my wife worry. I always make sure to get to bed at a reasonable hour. 

But, um... lately, it hasn't been the easiest. I don't want to make it sound like a huge problem, but... I just end up lying there for a while. I try to relax, but I keep replaying things from work in my head, just staring up at the ceiling. And then... well, even when I do finally drift off, I seem to be waking up really early. Like, around three or four in the morning. And I just can't seem to get back to sleep after that. I just lie there, already feeling worn out, and... well, kind of dreading having to get up and face the day. 

I feel terrible complaining about it, I know a lot of people have trouble sleeping sometimes. It's just a phase, right? I'm sure it's nothing to be too concerned about. I hope I'm explaining it clearly enough for you... does that make sense?
Ruben, have you ever felt this way before—like this heavy, hollow feeling and losing interest in things—or is this the first time you've experienced something like this?

Well, I... no, I don't think so. I've always prided myself on being a pretty upbeat guy. You know, working in sales, you kind of have to keep a smile on your face and keep pushing forward for the clients. I never want to be the guy bringing everyone else down. 

So... no, this is really the first time I've ever felt quite like this. I mean, everybody has a bad day here and there, and I really don't want to sound like I'm making a mountain out of a molehill, but... it's never been this heavy before. Usually, I can just shake things off and get right back to it. 

I hope that's okay to say? It's honestly a little embarrassing to be dealing with this for the first time at my age, and I don't want to be a difficult case for you. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right background so you have what you need. Does that help answer your question?
Ruben, have you ever felt so low or hopeless that you’ve thought about hurting yourself or wished you were dead?

Well, I... I really don't want you to think I'm crazy or anything. I know I have a lot to be thankful for—a beautiful wife, great kids. I always try to focus on the positive, I really do. I'd never want to do anything to hurt them or cause a scene. 

But, um... if I'm being completely honest, and I know I need to be honest with you... it's just been so hard lately. I haven't made any plans or anything like that, please don't worry about that. But... sometimes, I've just been having these thoughts. Thoughts that maybe... maybe they would just be better off if I didn't wake up in the morning. Like I'm just a burden to them now. 

It's awful to even say out loud, and I feel so guilty for even letting my mind go there. It actually scares me a bit, to be honest. I just... I don't quite trust myself the way I used to, and I hate that I'm even bringing it up. I know it sounds terrible, and I'm so sorry if that's alarming. I just want to make sure I'm giving you all the pieces so you can do your job. Is it... is it somewhat normal for people feeling this down to have thoughts like that? I just hope I'm not beyond help.
